subject: Regional connectivity impact — temporary egress swivel & repointing instructions
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@stratotech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regional connectivity impact — temporary egress swivel & repointing instructions

Hi Sanjay / Ops Team,

Quick note from the incident desk: we’re seeing elevated token latency (and some request failures) originating from our US and EU edge clusters that require customers to temporarily repoint egress to alternate endpoints while we enact a regional kernel rollout. This is targeted to specific cloud regions and is not an account-level outage, but it can impact inference latency for requests routed through affected edges.

What we’ve done so far:
- Identified a kernel-level regression on certain instance types that increases P99 token latency for short-sequence workloads.
- Scoped the problem to a subset of US-east and EU-west egress paths. APAC shows intermittent elevation; we are treating it as a separate but related symptom.
- Rolled a guarded rollback to a previous kernel on a fraction of capacity and started traffic drain/shift.

Immediate customer actions we recommend (low-risk, reversible):
1) Short-term egress swivel: update your SDK region preference to one of the unaffected endpoints below (example curl and SDK flags provided). This moves traffic away from impacted egress points and preserves low latency.
   - Primary fallback endpoints: api.redwood.inference.us-west-2, api.redwood.inference.eu-central-1
2) Reduce DNS TTL for your client-side resolver to 60s if you have a long TTL — this speeds repointing.
3) If you use pinned model versions, ensure you have a compatible fallback variant (we can provide a small variant list for your pinned models).

Example (curl):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.inference.us-west-2/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"ping"}'

Example SDK override (node):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({apiBaseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.inference.us-west-2'});

I’ve attached a short checklist and a diagnostics bundle request if you want us to pull per-connection logs (diagnostic-log-20260529.txt). If you prefer, we can run a guided repoint with your SRE over a screenshare.

We will update the status page as we progress: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2026-05-regional-egress

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll push an update in ~60 minutes or when we complete the next rollback window.

— Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

Attachments: egress-switch-checklist.pdf, client-reroute-sample-configs.yaml
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@stratotech.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional connectivity impact — temporary egress swivel & repointing instructions

Thanks Michael — we’re seeing increased 5xxs and a spike in P99 from our US-east origin pool starting ~07:45 PDT. A few quick items:
- We have a DNS TTL of 300s at the moment for our internal resolver. We can drop it to 60s immediately.
- We pin a large batch job to a specific model version; can you confirm the fallback variants you recommend?

Also, if you have a short checklist for connection validation post-switch (IP allowlist, certificate thumbprints, expected response headers), that would be great. If this will impact SLAs we need to track it on our side for the incident review.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Sr. Platform Engineer, StratoTech
ops@stratotech.com
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@stratotech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional connectivity impact — temporary egress swivel & repointing instructions

On 2026-05-30 08:46 -07:00, Sanjay Rao wrote:
> Thanks Michael — we’re seeing increased 5xxs and a spike in P99 from our US-east origin pool starting ~07:45 PDT. A few quick items:
> - We have a DNS TTL of 300s at the moment for our internal resolver. We can drop it to 60s immediately.
> - We pin a large batch job to a specific model version; can you confirm the fallback variants you recommend?

Thanks — good call lowering your TTL. Quick notes on your asks:
- Recommended fallback variants: for redwood-v1 use redwood-v1-legacy and redwood-v1-quantized-8k as safe fallbacks; they maintain behavior for short sequences and have verified throughput profiles.
- Connection validation checklist (short):
  * TLS: certificate chain unchanged; verify cert SHA256 thumbprint in header X-Redwood-Cert-SHA256.
  * IPs: no new egress IPs expected for the DNS-based switch (we only change edge selection).
  * Headers: expect X-Redwood-Edge and X-Redwood-Request-Id present in successful responses.

If you prefer an automated route we can set up a temporary route policy on your account to prefer api.redwood.inference.us-west-2; this will be removed after the rollback window. Let me know and I’ll open a short-lived route change (we’ll need an authorized approver).

I’ve attached sample client config for the repoint (client-reroute-sample-configs.yaml). I’ll loop Rishi for follow-up telemetry and Laura for credit/SLA impact tracking.

— Michael

Attachments: client-reroute-sample-configs.yaml
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: follow-up required — targeted kernel regression (US/EU)

Team — quick internal note to capture tasks from the customer-facing thread with StratoTech (SUP-45291):
- Rishi: pull per-connection traces for StratoTech between 2026-05-30T07:30 and 2026-05-30T08:30 PDT and attach to the ticket. I’ve already requested diagnostics from their side (see diagnostic-log-20260529.txt). Prioritize any kernel stack traces and scheduling metrics.
- Laura: please start an SLA impact calc for StratoTech (P99 latency and 5xx counts) and prepare a courtesy credit proposal if the incident meets the SLA breach thresholds. We should also prepare a brief summary for postmortem (~200-400 words) focused on the rollback decision and steps we took for repoint.

Current status: we rolled a partial rollback (10% of affected capacity) and are observing a reduction in token latency on the rolled hosts; full rollback scheduled in the 12:00 PDT window pending validation.

I’ll keep you posted; tagging jira INF-7832 for trace artifacts.

— Michael
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@stratotech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-31T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: rollback completed, recommended post-incident steps and credit

Hi Sanjay,

Final update: the full rollback to the previous kernel completed at 14:20 PDT and we validated end-to-end request flows for your account. Your P99 has returned to baseline in our checks.

Post-incident items we recommend for StratoTech:
- Keep the temporary SDK endpoint override for 24 hours and then revert to your prior setting during a low-traffic window.
- Re-instate DNS TTL to your normal value after 10 minutes of stable traffic to avoid flapping.
- Run the quick validation in the attached checklist after you revert: verify X-Redwood-Edge header, check 2xx rate, and sample latencies.

As discussed internally, Laura will follow up on a courtesy credit if thresholds are met; I’m copying her here. Rishi attached traces to the ticket (SUP-45291) and INF-7832 for the postmortem.

Again, apologies for the disruption and thanks for the rapid coordination. If you want a short postmortem call (15–20m) tomorrow we can schedule with our incidents team.

— Michael

Attachments: diagnostic-log-20260529.txt, egress-switch-checklist.pdf
